# Soonhwan Kwon

## About Me

I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Political Science at Indiana University Bloomington. My research lies at the intersection of comparative politics, political economy, and public policy, with a primary focus on the political economy of housing.

My dissertation examines how housing policies shape citizens’ expectations about economic security, asset accumulation, and upward mobility, and how these expectations influence political attitudes and policy preferences. I approach housing policy as an institution that structures the relationship between households, markets, and the state.

My dissertation takes a comparative approach, examining South Korea alongside cases in Europe and the United States to understand how different housing and welfare systems shape political attitudes and economic expectations. Building on this work, my broader research agenda places greater emphasis on South Korea and East Asia while continuing to use cross-national comparison to study the development and political consequences of housing institutions.

I am particularly interested in how housing policy interacts with economic development, welfare provision, household asset formation, and patterns of homeownership. More broadly, my research engages questions of welfare development, household wealth, labor markets, and the political consequences of major economic and social policies.

Methodologically, I use quasi-experimental and longitudinal research designs, including Difference-in-Differences, Regression Discontinuity Design, panel data analysis, and fixed-effects models, to study the effects of policy change on political attitudes and behavior.

If you are interested in any of these research areas, please feel free to contact me.
